track_length_definition: track_length is conditioned on >=20 samples; all_segment_length includes every contiguous segment; track span is first-to-last converted sample plus one sample interval
area_source: shared-site union across recordings on a 0.25 m occupancy grid; smallest cells containing 75% of observations
cv_definition: last observed displacement extrapolated one canonical timestep at a time (Schöller et al. convention)
min_tca_definition: min_time_to_closest_approach_scene reports the time (relative to the last observed step) at which two agents' constant-velocity extrapolated tracks reach minimum separation, gated on that minimum being under 2*radius (a contact/collision event), following the OpenTraj TTC/DCA convention (references/opentraj/.../indicators/collision_energy.py). This is time to *closest approach*, not time to *first contact* (the earlier moment the gap first reaches 2*radius) -- OpenTraj itself calls this quantity "TTC", so the name is an inherited misnomer rather than a STEPS one; A2-016 renamed the STEPS field to state the definition instead. Three implementation details diverge from the OpenTraj port and are deliberately left unchanged: (1) times>=0 is required here where upstream requires times>0, (2) the relative-velocity denominator is regularised with >=1e-9 here versus upstream's +1e-6 additive term, and (3) velocity is derived from a 2-step finite difference of positions here rather than from stored vx,vy as upstream does.
sample_representations: OpenTraj analysis trajlets and 8+12 forecast windows are independent indices
